name: baseline
note: All three roles on the model used for the recorded baseline run (see README.md's key-results table). Kept as the control -- newer variants below are measured against this one.

name: prose-split
note: RETIRED 2026-08-17: qwen3-235b-a22b judged too low quality for continued use in the 2026-07-29 A/B (see dialogue-control-qwen's note below) -- never once called wuxia_corpus_search across the recorded run despite claiming tool-calling support. Not deleted so the retrieval_calls==0 finding stays attached to the entry that produced it; pass --variants prose-split to re-run it if a newer qwen3 release warrants revisiting.

name: cheap-ends
note: RETIRED 2026-08-17 (already broken as of the 2026-07-29 A/B run and never fixed): qwen3-30b-a3b fails 10/10 structured-output parses as writer/proof -- it prepends explanatory prose before the JSON object, which breaks CrewAI's beta.chat.completions.parse() before pipeline.py's coercion fallback chain runs. Qwen3 family judged too low quality for continued use; needs a different writer/proof model (and a newer, better qwen3 release, if revisited) before this variant is usable again.

name: dialogue-control-openai
note: RETIRED 2026-08-17: OpenAI models excluded from further evaluation per project decision (out of scope for this repo's per-token cost/quality goals). Was the control for prose-split -- established the tool-call-propensity ceiling under tool_choice="auto" (3.3 retrieval_calls avg, 0/10 zero-call runs) that qwen3-235b-a22b failed to approach. Kept for that historical reference; pass --variants dialogue-control-openai to re-run it.

name: dialogue-control-qwen
note: RETIRED 2026-08-17: qwen3-30b-a3b never once called wuxia_corpus_search (10/10 zero-call runs) despite OpenRouter's /models metadata claiming tool-calling support -- the finding that separated 'qwen family never calls the tool' from 'only the large MoE (prose-split) doesn't'. Qwen3 family judged too low quality for continued use; revisit if a newer qwen3 release changes this.

name: long-cheap
note: 2026-08-17: script-length feasibility A/B, arm 1. All six roles on deepseek-v4-flash-0731 (same family as baseline's deepseek-chat, so structural-output risk should be low) pinned to OpenRouter's Decart endpoint -- see eval/model_prices.json (fetched 2026-08-17: $0.0603/$0.1206 per 1M prompt/completion, ~4.3x/8.5x cheaper than deepseek-chat's default routing). Candidate replacement baseline if script_length=medium quality holds up. Set LLM_PROVIDER_ONLY=Decart (or pass --pipeline-mode layered with this variant) to actually route there -- see .env.example.

name: long-prose
note: 2026-08-17: script-length feasibility A/B, arm 2. Mechanical roles (extractor/beat_expander/writer/proof) on the cheap deepseek-v4-flash-0731 (Decart), dialogue/scene_writer on z-ai/glm-5.2 (Novita) for prose quality -- mirrors prose-split's split-spend shape, but with models actually verified for tool-calling reliability instead of assumed from provider metadata (see prose-split's retirement note above: verify retrieval_calls for this variant too, don't assume). NOTE: glm-5.2's Novita price moved between two fetches minutes apart while building eval/model_prices.json (0.3388->0.7406 per 1M prompt) -- re-run scripts/refresh_prices.py before trusting a cost comparison involving this variant.

name: long-mimo
note: 2026-08-17: script-length feasibility A/B, arm 3. All six roles on xiaomi/mimo-v2.5 pinned to OpenRouter's GMICloud endpoint ($0.119/$0.238 per 1M prompt/completion as of 2026-08-17, 1M+ context) -- a Chinese-native model at a similar price point to deepseek-v4-flash-0731, testing whether that matters for 武俠語感 at longer script lengths.
